Ensure the names of an object meet expectations

Source: R/stabilize_names.R
stabilize_names.Rd

Validate and optionally convert only the names of an object. The class and values of x are left alone, so this is useful for objects (such as S3 classes or factors) that you don't want to convert or check. stabilise_names() is a synonym of stabilize_names().

Usage

stabilize_names(
  x,
  ...,
  allowed_names = NULL,
  spec = NULL,
  required = NULL,
  allow_duplicate_names = FALSE,
  x_arg = caller_arg(x),
  call = caller_env()
)

stabilise_names(
  x,
  ...,
  allowed_names = NULL,
  spec = NULL,
  required = NULL,
  allow_duplicate_names = FALSE,
  x_arg = caller_arg(x),
  call = caller_env()
)

Arguments

x

The object to stabilize.

...

Arguments passed to methods.

allowed_names

(character) The permitted names. If supplied, x must be named (every element must have a non-empty name), and every name must be in this set. NULL (default), NA, or character(0) skip the check.

spec

(function) A single stabilizer or conversion function, such as a to_* function (to_chr(), etc.), a stabilize_* function (stabilize_chr(), etc.), or a function produced by a specify_*() call (specify_chr(), etc.). If supplied, x must be named (every element must have a non-empty name), and spec is applied to names(x). The result becomes the names of the returned object. NULL (default) skips the check.

required

(character) Names that must be present in x (after applying spec, if any). NULL (default) or character() skip the check.

allow_duplicate_names

(logical(1)) Should x be allowed to have duplicate names?

x_arg

(character(1)) The name of the object being stabilized to use in error messages. The automatic value will work in most cases, or pass it through from higher-level functions to make error messages clearer in unexported functions.

call

(environment) The execution environment to mention as the source of error messages.

Value

x with stabilized names, or an error condition with classes <stbl-error>, <stbl-condition>, <rlang_error>, <error>, <condition>, and a specific class by failure mode:

  • <stbl-error-bad_named> when allowed_names or spec is supplied and x is not fully named.

  • <stbl-error-allowed_names> when a name is not in allowed_names.

  • <stbl-error-duplicate_names> when duplicate names are present and allow_duplicate_names = FALSE.

  • <stbl-error-missing_element> when a name in required is absent.

  • Errors from spec when a name does not satisfy it.

See also

Other names functions: specify_names()

Other stabilization functions: assert_contains(), assert_not(), assert_present(), stabilize_all_of(), stabilize_any_of(), stabilize_arg(), stabilize_chr(), stabilize_chr_scalar(), stabilize_date(), stabilize_date_scalar(), stabilize_dbl(), stabilize_dbl_scalar(), stabilize_df(), stabilize_dttm(), stabilize_dttm_scalar(), stabilize_dur(), stabilize_dur_scalar(), stabilize_fct(), stabilize_fct_scalar(), stabilize_int(), stabilize_int_scalar(), stabilize_lgl(), stabilize_lgl_scalar(), stabilize_lst(), stabilize_one_of(), stabilize_time(), stabilize_time_scalar(), to_chr(), to_chr_scalar(), to_date(), to_date_scalar(), to_dbl(), to_dbl_scalar(), to_dttm(), to_dttm_scalar(), to_dur(), to_dur_scalar(), to_fct(), to_fct_scalar(), to_int(), to_int_scalar(), to_lgl(), to_lgl_scalar(), to_time(), to_time_scalar()

Examples

# Names are checked, but the class and values are untouched
stabilize_names(c(a = 1, b = 2))
#> a b 
#> 1 2 

# Duplicate names are rejected by default
try(stabilize_names(c(a = 1, a = 2)))
#> Error in eval(expr, envir) : 
#>   `c(a = 1, a = 2)` must not contain duplicate names.
#> ✖ Duplicate name: "a"
stabilize_names(c(a = 1, a = 2), allow_duplicate_names = TRUE)
#> a a 
#> 1 2 

# Require specific names
try(stabilize_names(c(a = 1, b = 2), required = c("a", "c")))
#> Error in eval(expr, envir) : 
#>   `c(a = 1, b = 2)` must contain name "c".

# Restrict names to an allowed set
try(stabilize_names(c(a = 1, z = 2), allowed_names = c("a", "b")))
#> Error in eval(expr, envir) : 
#>   `c(a = 1, z = 2)` must have names from the allowed set.
#> ℹ Allowed names: "a" and "b".
#> ✖ Unexpected location: 2
#> ✖ Unexpected name: "z".

# Convert or validate the names with a spec
stabilize_names(c(a = 1, b = 2), spec = toupper)
#> A B 
#> 1 2 
try(stabilize_names(c(a = 1, B = 2), spec = specify_chr(regex = "^[a-z]$")))
#> Error in eval(expr, envir) : 
#>   `names(c(a = 1, B = 2))` must match the regex pattern "^[a-z]$"
#> ✖ Some values fail the check.
#> ✖ Location: 2
#> ✖ Value: B
